title: Antonio da Trezzo, King Ferrante's camp, to Francesco Sforza: cipher slip of 8 Sept 1464 (BnF italien 1590, f. 392; catalogue 1320)

system.summary: Continuous signs, no word division, about 1.7 clear letters per sign: letter signs, syllable signs and common-word signs (aligner: qa et, t che, h' non, Lu per, 4π er, 4e es, ar en, 8 al, δπ in, z ad, hr ell, L^a sua, L^u la S.V.), vowel strokes written after or above a base sign.
system.sibling_key: rebuilt from the cipher letter ff. 283r-284r and its contemporary translation ff. 281r-282r in the same volume

prior_solution.where: No decipherment of f. 392 known: no DECODE record, nothing in Tomokiyo or Lasry, no printed Dispacci sforzeschi da Napoli volume for 1464 (catalogue vetting of 11 Nov 2026; re-checked 14 Nov 2026). The sibling letter of 16 July 1464 has its contemporary translation in the volume (ff. 281r-282r).

conditions.human_role: Arya Sanketbhai Patel ran the session, chose the route (rebuild the key from the sibling letter rather than wait for a DECODE login) and checked the DECODE listing. An AI agent transcribed, aligned, decoded and wrote the notes. No palaeographer checked the transcriptions.
models: AI coding agent (model not named by the contributor)

solution.what: Prior-art re-check (catalogue vetting re-read; repository searched for italien 1590 and Trezzo): no decipherment of f. 392 known.
DECODE key sheets of ASMi Sforzesco cart. 1597 (one of R5329-R5344 is Antonio da Trezzo's): record pages are a login shell from this session; not reached.
f. 392, 13 lines, 398 sign tokens in 68 base shapes (c392.txt), one pass before any key.
Syllabic signs: f. 283r line 1 has 25 signs for about 48 letters of its translation; shapes pair a base sign with a written vowel (L^a / L^u / Lo, δa / δu / δo, 4e / 4o / 4a).

The sibling cipher letter of 16 July 1464, ff. 283r (40 lines), 283v (39), 284r (11), deskewed and cut into strips (c283.txt, c284.txt), and its contemporary translation ff. 281r-282r expanded to 4,677 letters (t281_full.txt).
Soft-EM aligner (targets/duben1764/fb.py) on f. 283r lines 1-26 against translation lines 1-22: top-share 0.335 (superscripts split 0.319, dropped 0.297; plaintext cut to 60-95 %: 0.32-0.35).

Same plaintext enciphered in a synthetic 70-sign syllabic code (control.py): clean 0.993, 20 % misread signs 0.789, 40 % 0.611; with the clear running 25 % past the cipher, 0.297; free-end and tail-cost variants of the aligner fail the noisy controls. The partial-letter run is therefore not decidable; both ends must be fixed.

Whole letter, cipher 283r-284r.10 (2,792 tokens) against the translation to 'del tucto' (4,677 letters), both ends fixed: top-share 0.589 (controls at the same size: 20 % noise 0.787, 40 % noise 0.611). Key key_full_v1.json; frequent signs consistent (qa et 54/62, ot d 70/89, 4π er 67/83, h' non 15/16, hr ell 8/8), the commonest label p split between t, r and p.

f. 392 decoded with key_full_v1.json (top values, decode392_keytop.txt) and refined by it-cinquecento score with the key as prior (refine.py, lambda 3, decode392_refined.txt): Italian fragments that fit the context ('restitutione', 'quali hanno effecto', 'desiderio essere', 'alcuno che', 'la S.V.', 'amici', 'nella'), no sentence holds. Decoded, not read; no strict count made.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt by aligning the sibling cipher letter of 16 July 1464 (ff. 283r-284r) with its contemporary translation in the same volume (ff. 281r-282r); f. 392 decodes with it into Italian fragments only.
outcome.notes: Status in progress. f. 392 decoded, not read (Italian fragments, no sentence). Key partial: the alignment fits at the level of a 40 %-noise control; the transcription labels lump shapes the key distinguishes. Open: re-transcription with finer sign distinctions; the DECODE Trezzo key sheet (R5329-R5344, login) and Cerioni 1970 untested.
